title: Make bigger = better: the 8a growth ladder (3M -> 10M -> 30M -> hundreds of millions)

brief.state:
Stage 8a (is bigger better for B2?) is sealed (8A-SPEC-2026-10-07.md, PR #50, addenda A to G) and has not run. Nothing has been measured above B2's 3.3M on the skills data. Every size point in the history is a different design, a different dataset, or one seed: PR #18's +1.9 is an older frozen-1.2B core (9.0 to 35.8M, English new kinds, CI -0.95 to +4.77); B1's 10.9M students ran on TEACH/GEN and were flat on new kinds; the plain 3.2M vs 10.8M calibration is one seed.

B2 baseline (q33, seeds 200-205, 24k updates, 3,302,481 params; recomputed from RESULT.json): pooled-5 74.0 (seed sd 0.6), plain_tf 53.7 (B2 +20.3), plain_tf_steps 67.1 (B2 +6.9, ahead 6 of 6). Chain-5 99.4-99.7. Weak points: variant 34.7 (only +4.8 over plain_tf_steps), held-out kinds 1.6%, fewshot_number_rule (-14.9 vs plain_tf_steps). Leak (loops:0, in_dist) 0-10.8, over the limit of 5 on seeds 201 and 203. Sixteen rounds cost -0.85 pooled.

Shape arithmetic (checked against two documented counts): at width 256 a block adds 1,158,604 params, so the 10M band admits only 8 blocks (10,254,105). The spec's 10-12 blocks would be 12.6-14.9M. At width 384 (mlp 6.0) a block adds 2,957,952, so the 30M band admits 9 blocks (28.6M); the spec's 14-16 blocks would be 43-49M.

Plan: rungs 3M, 10M, 30M; a fixed 38% own text and 62% FineWeb-Edu cloze rows; pools 60M (3M and 10M share it) and 190M; seeds 400-405 at each rung; arms B2, plain_tf_steps (C0 if it passes) and an LLM-recipe arm not yet built. Marks: +3.0 per rung with CI above 0; lead over plain not down more than 1.0; at 30M, +3.0 on 5 of 6 seeds; good enough means 3M at least 72.0 and 30M at least pythia-31m +2.0. No 30M rung if 10M minus 3M is below 0. Runs on BensPC. Estimates (suggested): 3M about 9 h, 10M about a day, 30M 4-5 days; 30M waits for Ben.

Risks: the 10M-to-30M step changes width, learning rate, updates and pool at once. Cloze answers are mostly absent from the prompt, so B2 must spell them with its char generator, which was trained only on short answers. B2 still has hand parts (regex spans, in-forward executor, str() renderer, a 7-step cap that gives 528 train rows no program), so 8a measures today's design. The 30M shape probably needs micro-batches to fit 16 GB (suggested).

distinct.title: Cache frozen Gemma token states
distinct.summary: EGE re-runs the 271M frozen encoder on every batch (only the last call is memoised), yet each training prompt is seen about 31 times. Store each prompt's token-level 768-d states once, keyed by the exact string Gemma sees, and gather per batch. The trained model and its math do not change; the saving could be about half the update time.
distinct.change: models/eg.py FrozenEG.encode checks an on-disk fp16 memory-mapped cache keyed by (EG_REV, tokenizer hash, PREFIX + prompt); a miss runs Gemma and writes it. distinct.why: EGE is 3.65 steps/s vs R0's 7.24 in the same queue, so the frozen forward is roughly half the update (suggested). Gemma's states do not depend on the reader's window or the batch (padding changes at most 0.0005), so a key on the exact string is legal. Build cost about 2e15 FLOP for ~7M tokens (suggested), minutes on the 5070 Ti.

distinct.title: Model-chosen blanks on web text
distinct.summary: Instead of blanking one uniformly drawn word per chunk, the model scores four candidate words by its own loss on each blanked version and samples one in proportion to that loss, so one chunk yields many different questions and the data keeps pace with the model. The true word in the text is the check. Each chunk is visited at most four times and no word is asked twice, keeping the repeat rule.
distinct.change: Replace the uniform blank draw in the 8a cloze builder (cloze.py, not in checkout): per visit draw k=4 eligible words not yet asked for that chunk; score each by B2's own loss with that word blanked (no backward); sample one proportional to loss; visit cap 4. Eligible words 3-8 letters while GEN_MAX=8, excluded share reported (or the median-surprise variant of 8 candidates at update 2,000). Targets stay the blanked word. 0 params; +50-100% per update (suggested).
distinct.why: A 280-letter chunk has roughly 25-30 eligible words (untested), so one text supports many questions; uniform blanks include trivial function words and unguessable names. Bigger models predict more of each chunk, so a loss-weighted choice keeps finding blanks worth asking without new text. Risks: picks names or rare words (spelling, not skills), prefers copyable repeats, biases blank length; guards test each.

Nearly all are zero-compute reanalyses, CPU probes on the six saved q33 B2 checkpoints (code/b2ckpt, verified present, 13.2 MB each, seed identity shown only for 200-202), or 2-seed screens of 2-8 PC hours. The central finding is that no B2 result yet shows bigger is better on the skills data, and the 8a mark of +3.0 per rung is statistically demanding (about 25% pass at a true +3 for two rungs). The most valuable moves are the cheap decision aids. First, re-power the first-look gate and add the missing plain-10M arm (the rented boxes run only the 3M pair and B2D). Second, run a block-use census to learn whether added depth is used, which decides the 30M shape (the spec's 10-12 and 14-16 blocks do not fit the parameter bands; 8 blocks at width 256 and 9 at mlp 6.0 or 11 at mlp 4.8 at width 384 do). Third, run a spelling gate, because 62% of the 8a web rows ask a parallel 8-letter generator to write 3-12 letter words (13 registers fit the existing place table, so the pilot needs only one constant). Fourth, cut B2's step time, since B2 is about 4x plain per update at 8a caps and the 30M rung is about 13-14 h a seed. I verified the workspace key/value premise in ledger.py, the existence of the checkpoints, the pool resolution (addendum I1: 3M and 10M share the 60M pool) and the speed table (addendum I2). Corrections applied: the cap-truncation hypothesis is refuted by LIMIT-COUNTS, odd_one_out has no vocab rows, the variant split has 33 families, the executor-bound set is a 50% coverage cut, and the first look runs on rented 5090s. Two ideas were dropped (rule 10 and cost). The variant-data ideas probably overlap another area. Missing: any test of the size claim at 30M that is cheap, and a plan for collecting the first-look checkpoints before the boxes are destroyed.
